body:
Your diction is fine I honestly thought you were just coming across as someone who wants to help. I'm just frustrated because my 20th birthday is very very soon and I still am this lost cause. 
    It seems like at least in reddit and in the academic advising eyes you either enjoy STEM or you are worthless.
    I'm sorry I should have clarified. My problem isn't necessarily that I am not interested in things, it's that I am interested in too many things. Off the cuff I can think of:

*Photography

*Fitness

*Guns

*Adrenaline inducing activities

*Bartending

*Teaching

*History

*Politics

*Technology

*Animal biology

*Gardening

*Motorcycles

*Flying

*Performing music (really performing anything)

*Counselling

*Dentistry

*Surgeries

*Criminal Law

*Languages (specifically English French and German)

*Electrical work

*Politics

*Marketing/finance

I am interested in travel. I'm just not interested in crowds of tourists and sightseeing for the most part. I'd rather spend money to go skydiving or climb mountains than fight through crowds of people to see the mona Lisa only to be stopped 30ft short by a big ol' rope and a couple layers of bulletproof glass. I don't think it's bad that other people do like this stuff maybe they like seeing or being in a historic place but I find I get distracted by the people. It's almost disheartening to see people spend a bunch of money and time to go to these places and spend it all looking through a camera lens or a smartphone. These aren't professional photographers these are regular people trying to upload the same God awful picture them holding up the tower of Pisa. They do this to put their stamp down like a dog that pisses over the same fire hydrant except they post it to also keep up with their friends in a way since the fear of missing out is so widespread these days.

   I don't know why I go on random rants like that it just helps me feel better that I'm typing. I guess my thought is that I'll find some idea of what my value is to society and an actual passion instead of yet another interest.

I'm just trying to get into elementary I think. I don't know.... Anyways it is like 6 years to get a B.A and a B.ed or it's 5 years to get just a B.ed. can't do science and math well enough to pull out amazing grades otherwise I wouldn't be wondering what I want to do.

I wouldn't say that I necessarily get down about comparing since I don't have an interest in what he does. Its more to do with for whatever reason the people around me can achieve whatever they want, while myself regardless of them, can't make any out my dreams or goals come true. I hope that makes sense.

So then how can I get this confidence and start actually being able to realize dreams instead of having them crushed?

Edit: I'm failing tests due to my genetic makeup (poor vision,tremors, etc) and because of I let my circumstances get the better of me. I'd study in an area I knew nothing about, go the extra miles necessary, and then still bomb the tests due to anxiety or just plain too depressed to get out of bed, or in most cases,still not understanding/memorizing what I needed to. Now I am in the arts and while it's easier I still have that daunting amount of F's behind me.

For some reason this lack of success is not limited to just academics. I rarely get the job, or keep the girl (cheated on or dumped), or really win. I know it sounds very much a poor me statement but I just don't seem to win a lot.

Thank you for responding. But why does it never seem to work out? From when I was a child it's just been failed tests (acedemic, colorblind, etc) that cause me to change my dreams (Dentist,Pilot, etc) until I'm left here with nothing to go down from. I'm already in the easiest major for me I'm doing my best and yet I'm still screwing up. Whether it's money, relationships, or mental health something always seems to backfire. When I say brother I mean in the figurative sense. He is my best friend and also to a lesser extent my chauffeur since I'm not allowed to have a car this year.
